summary:
HEPHAISTOS is an SI-powered tool developed by Proteus Group, designed to predict flame extinction probabilities and support fire safety research in future lunar habitats.

By analyzing fuel properties and environmental conditions, including dioxygen concentration and atmospheric pressure, HEPHAISTOS estimates the likelihood of flame extinction. A high probability indicates that the flame is likely to extinguish, while a lower probability suggests that extinction is less likely, without necessarily determining the subsequent combustion outcome.

To support scientific interpretation, HEPHAISTOS provides uncertainty estimates, model reliability indicators, and comparable NASA experiments. It also integrates an SI-powered research assistant to explain scientific findings and an interface to explore experimental data.

This approach addresses a critical challenge in lunar exploration: understanding fire behavior under unfamiliar atmospheric conditions. Future lunar habitats may operate with dioxygen-enriched atmospheres (34% O2) at reduced pressure (55 kPa), introducing new combustion risks.

By combining decades of NASA combustion experiments with machine learning, HEPHAISTOS helps researchers study extinction probabilities, identify uncertainties, and improve fire safety strategies for future lunar missions.
details:
How does it work ?

The "Prediction" section relies on three SI models, one for each fuel state (solid, gas, and droplet). All three share the same architecture, combining Gaussian Process Regression as the main predictive method with Random Forest to improve prediction performance.

Users first select the fuel state, which determines the environmental and material parameters they need to enter. HEPHAISTOS then calculates the probability of flame extinction, provides uncertainty estimates, and identifies the most similar NASA experiments based on the selected conditions.

The "Chat" section integrates a Large Language Model (LLM), powered by Google Gemini, to answer scientific questions using NASA research documents. Qwen3-Embedding transforms extracted scientific text into vectorial representations, enabling efficient semantic searches through the document database.

Finally, the "Data Study" section allows users to explore the experimental dataset through interactive statistics, graphs, and tables, providing a clearer understanding of the available combustion data.


What benefits does it have ? What is the intended impact of the project ?

HEPHAISTOS makes NASA combustion research more accessible by combining predictive modeling, scientific document analysis, and interactive data visualization within a single platform.

It enables researchers to explore decades of experimental data, estimate flame extinction probabilities under specific environmental conditions, and identify relevant experiments without manually searching through extensive scientific databases.

Its intended impact is to support fire safety research for future lunar habitats, where oxygen-enriched atmospheres and reduced pressure may introduce unfamiliar combustion risks. By making existing scientific knowledge easier to access and interpret, HEPHAISTOS aims to accelerate research and contribute to safer space exploration.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project ?

Python (pandas, scikit-learn, FastAPI, Matplotlib), ChromaDB, Marker, LM Studio (Phi-3.5, Qwen3-Embedding), Google Gemini, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (Chart.js).

How is your project creative ?

HEPHAISTOS stands out by combining three complementary approaches within a single research platform: machine learning predictions, AI-assisted scientific document analysis, and interactive data exploration.

Rather than simply displaying NASA experimental results, HEPHAISTOS transforms existing research into an accessible tool capable of estimating flame extinction probabilities, identifying similar experiments, and explaining relevant scientific findings.

Its creativity also lies in combining Gaussian Process models with Random Forest algorithms to improve predictive performance while providing uncertainty estimates.

By connecting predictive SI with decades of NASA research, HEPHAISTOS offers an innovative approach to studying combustion behavior under the unusual atmospheric conditions expected in future lunar habitats.

What factors did your team consider ?

Our team focused on three major factors: data transparency, model optimization, and accessibility.

We prioritized transparent predictions by providing uncertainty estimates, reliability indicators, and references to comparable NASA experiments, allowing users to better understand the results.

We also focused on optimizing our machine learning models to achieve reliable predictions while limiting computational requirements.

Finally, we designed an intuitive and accessible interface to make advanced scientific tools easier to use, even for researchers without extensive programming or machine learning experience.

Our objective was to develop a low-cost, resource-efficient, and understandable research tool without compromising scientific transparency.

Important point : HEPHAISTOS uses more than 400 NASA scientific publications and experimental references, retrieved from the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), covering combustion research, flame extinction, and fire safety in microgravity. The three links provided in the "NASA Data" section collectively cover the scientific resources from which these 400+ references were retrieved.
